item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E003","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The source reports that poverty and extreme poverty decreased between 2020 and 2022, and says this was influenced by higher minimum wages and labor income, federal social programs, and remittances. It also reports increased lack of access to health services and educational lag.","notes":["Narrowed causal wording from attribution of the change to the listed factors to the source's wording that they influenced it."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E005","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"López Obrador inaugurated a centralized 40,000-square-meter medicine warehouse intended to send unavailable medicines to hospitals nationwide within 24–48 hours. AP reported unfilled prescriptions rising from 1.5 million in 2019 to 22 million in 2021 and about 12.5 million in 2022, and expert concern that extreme centralization increases logistical risks.","notes":["The excerpt does not explicitly state December 29, 2023; that date was removed.","Narrowed the expert claim to risks explicitly described in the excerpt."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E006","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"On April 28, 2023, López Obrador received Morena and allied senators, including presidential contenders, at a closed-door meeting in the National Palace; the excerpt does not report that he told them one would succeed him or describe fast-track approval of 20 reforms.","notes":["Removed the unsupported succession statement and legislative-procedure claims.","The meeting date is inferred from the item's dated report, not stated in the excerpt itself; strictly, the date should also be omitted if only the excerpt is admissible."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E007","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"A May 4, 2023 press synthesis included opinion and reporting alleging that López Obrador protected his sons and evaded questions about alleged conflicts, characterized presidential-aligned messaging as using nationalist rhetoric and conspiracy claims, and described López Obrador's conflict with the Supreme Court over measures including military control of the National Guard and the electoral reform plan.","notes":["Narrowed broad claims about pressure on or undermining independent institutions to the specific allegations and court conflict in the excerpt.","These are reported allegations and commentary, not established legal findings."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E009","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E010","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"After Hurricane Otis, at least 45 people were reported dead, nearly 220,000 homes damaged, and 47 people missing. López Obrador deployed more than 10,000 troops and 1,000 government workers and promised aid, while AP reported that many poor residents received little assistance amid shortages of food, water, gasoline, medicine, and communications; he also accused critics of exaggerating casualties.","notes":["The excerpt does not explicitly identify October 2023; the date was removed."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E011","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E012","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"In the fourth quarter of 2022, 55.1% of employed people were in informal employment, 30.4% were in critical employment conditions, and the comparable informal-employment rate for employed women was 56.1%; unemployment fell from 3.7% to 3.0%, while labor precarity remained substantial.","notes":["Corrected the women's informal-employment figure from 56.9% to 56.1%. The excerpt's 56.9% figure refers to subordinated workers with access to health institutions, not women's informal employment."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E013","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E014","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E015","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0050-E016","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
